Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for attaching the drafts. Short answers up front: yes, we can accept an agent-signed submission, but we need the authorization to meet certain minimum elements before we can treat an agent-signed W-9 as valid for 1099/1096 purposes. Details below and next steps.

Required documents (acceptable as PDF uploads):
- Completed W-9 (company name, EIN, tax classification). The payee name on the W-9 must match the name associated with the EIN.
- Agent Authorization Letter on company letterhead signed by an officer (name/title) delegating authority to the agent. The letter should include the agent's full name, company, and a copy of the agent's government ID.
- Evidence of authorization: either (a) scanned officer signature + ID, or (b) notarized agent authorization letter. Notarization is preferred when the signatory is external to the company.

For 1099 purposes: because you indicate "C-Corp", we will not issue a Form 1099-NEC to a C-Corp. However we still need a valid W-9 on file to ensure the EIN/name match and to clear the invoice for payment. If your entity type is different (LLC, disregarded entity, single-member), please include the exact classification on the W-9.

Secure upload: we have a temporary secure intake URL we can share for documents containing PII. Please upload signed documents there (DocuSign is also acceptable). I'll copy the secure link below. If you prefer DocuSign, please route final signed docs to treasury@redwood.com.

Secure upload (expires in 7 days): https://redwood.example/secure-upload/HL-4327
DocuSign (optional): https://docusign.example/abc123

Next steps/timeline:
- You upload completed W-9 + agent authorization + ID to the secure link.
- Our revenue ops (Marissa) will validate EIN/name match and classification (1 business day).
- Once validated, we route to AP for payment scheduling (Ben). Payments typically process on our next run (Net 30 from invoice receipt) unless an exception is requested.

If you'd like, we can accept a scanned driver license as the ID for the agent in lieu of notarization for the first-time submission, but we'll require notarization for recurring or high-dollar payees.

Let me know if that works and I'll confirm once I see the upload.

Best,
